caption: Psalm 9 and Acts share striking language about judging the world justly. Acts may specify Jesus as God’s agent—but it never identifies the psalm as a prediction.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 9 predict Jesus as judge? Psalm 9 says the LORD judges the world justly. Acts says God will judge through an appointed, risen man.
slides.body: Psalm 9 says the LORD judges the world justly. Acts says God will judge through an appointed, risen man.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 9 predict Jesus as judge?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 9:7-10: He judges the world with justice; He governs the people with equity.
slides.body: He judges the world with justice; He governs the people with equity.
slides.heading: Ps 9:7-10

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Acts 17:31, BSB: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
slides.body: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed. He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.”
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Acts 17:31

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The wording is strikingly close Christians see Jesus carrying out God’s own judgment. That makes the passages fit together well.
slides.body: Christians see Jesus carrying out God’s own judgment. That makes the passages fit together well.
slides.heading: The wording is strikingly close

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Acts never cites the psalm Psalm 9 names God as judge and says nothing about a risen human agent. The shared theme is not a distinct forecast.
slides.body: Psalm 9 names God as judge and says nothing about a risen human agent. The shared theme is not a distinct forecast.
slides.heading: But Acts never cites the psalm

title: Judging the world justly
